workflow.description: Deliver an epic as file-owning tasks in dependency waves, then one integration review. A claim ledger tracks each task; it stops after the task plan for your approval and never commits.
workflow.whenToUse: args: { epic: "<the epic>", tasks?: <the approved tasks array from the first run>, continueOnFailure?: false, maxRounds?: 3 }. The first run returns TASKS_READY with the tasks; run again with args.tasks to build them. Each task runs the feature-delivery stages for its class, then a fresh acceptance check; a failed task blocks its dependants, and the run stops at the first failure unless continueOnFailure is true. Any stop short of DONE returns an escalation; commit each task yourself with the dev-git-workflow skill. Files under .git, .claude, .codex, .agents, .github and other protected paths, and instruction files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, are out of reach: a change to one stops the run, so a human edits them outside any workflow.

phases.title: Plan
phases.detail: A read-only planner splits the epic into tasks; stops for approval unless args.tasks is given

phases.title: Test first
phases.detail: Per task: the test writer adds or edits only the task's test files

phases.title: Test check
phases.detail: Per task: a read-only test reviewer runs the tests; red for add, change and fix, green for refactor

phases.title: Implement
phases.detail: Per task: the implementer changes only the task's owned files

phases.title: Recheck
phases.detail: Per task: a read-only test reviewer runs the tests again; all must pass

phases.title: Acceptance
phases.detail: After each wave: one fresh read-only check per task runs its acceptance command, in parallel

phases.title: Review
phases.detail: Integration: fresh reviewers per dimension over the whole epic, every round

phases.title: Verify
phases.detail: Integration: two refuters per finding; both must refute to kill it

phases.title: Fix
phases.detail: Integration: the implementer fixes only the confirmed findings, inside the epic's files

waves.returns: { verdict: TASKS_READY | DONE | BLOCKED | INCOMPLETE | FINDINGS, ledger, waves, history, stop_reason, escalation?, changed_files_reported, changed_files_observed, tasks? }
waves.escalation_action: Stop and hand the open items to a human. Nothing was committed; review the working tree, commit each done task with the dev-git-workflow skill, or discard the change. To retry, run /epic-delivery again with args.tasks set to the tasks still open.
waves.ready_action: Review the tasks. To build them, run /epic-delivery again with the same epic and with args.tasks set to the approved tasks array.

planner.title: Plan
planner.task: Split the epic into tasks that can each be built, tested and committed alone. Give each task a short id (letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore), a goal, a class (add, change, fix or refactor), the ids it depends_on, the owned_files it may change, the test_files it may add or edit, acceptance checks that can fail, and one acceptance_command that runs those checks. Each file belongs to one task only: if two tasks need one file, merge them. For fix, state failure_reason; for change, list old_assertions. Never plan a file under .git, .claude, .codex, .agents or .github, or an instruction file such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

acceptance.title: Acceptance
acceptance.task: Run the task's acceptance_command exactly as given, once, and report it in command. Set passed to true only when the command succeeds and every acceptance check holds; quote the deciding output line in evidence.

waves.integration_task: Review the combined change of every task in the epic as one diff: how the tasks fit together, not each task alone.

owned_files.description: Every non-test file this task may change; no other task may own one

test_files.description: Every test file this task may add or edit; no other task may own one

acceptance_command.description: One shell command that runs the acceptance checks
